 The United States has taken another significant step towards strengthening its military installations. The country aims to boost force protection capabilities in the Middle East as it has awarded a contract worth more than $6.9 million for advanced radar systems designed to detect and track unmanned aerial threats. 
The contract, awarded by the Department of War’s Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401) to CHAOS 1 Inc., will provide Vanquish Prime advanced radar systems to support counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS) operations within the US Central Command (CENTCOM) area of responsibility. 
 Strengthening detection and tracking
 The step supports JIATF-401’s efforts to rapidly deliver operationally relevant C-UAS capabilities to the warfighter, strengthening detection and tracking as part of a layered defense against evolving unmanned aircraft threats . The radar systems will provide long-range detection and tracking capabilities to improve situational awareness and help U.S. forces respond more effectively to aerial threats, according to a press release.
By aligning targeted acquisitions with operational requirements, JIATF-401 is working to equip warfighters with integrated C-UAS capabilities that address threats across the detection and defeat process. Advanced radar systems provide a critical layer within this approach, helping forces identify and track potential threats and supporting a coordinated defense alongside other C-UAS technologies, as per the release.
 Threat from unmanned systems is real
 “This acquisition is a testament to our commitment to providing the warfighter with the most advanced capabilities available,” said Lt. Col. Matthew Strohman, JIATF-401’s Capability Manager for Mobile C-UAS. 
“The threat from unmanned systems is real and constantly evolving. By equipping our forces in CENTCOM with state-of-the-art technology, we are ensuring they have the decisive edge needed to protect our personnel and secure our strategic interests. This is about delivering the right tools at the speed of relevance.”
Under the contract, CHAOS 1 Inc. will deliver Vanquish Prime radar systems to designated locations across the CENTCOM region. The agreement also includes training and technological support to facilitate the integration and operational deployment of the systems.
The radar systems are expected to provide an important detection and tracking layer within the broader US counter-UAS architecture. Their deployment will help military personnel maintain improved awareness of unmanned aircraft activity and strengthen the ability to identify potential threats to personnel, military installations and other critical assets.
The acquisition reflects the changing nature of aerial threats, particularly the increasing employment of relatively inexpensive unmanned aircraft by state and non-state actors. Such systems can present significant challenges to conventional air-defence networks, making early detection and reliable tracking essential components of military force protection. 
Modern counter-UAS operations require more than a single detection or interception capability. They depend on the integration of surveillance, detection, tracking and response technologies to address different categories of unmanned aerial threats.
Within this framework, advanced radar systems serve as a critical component by providing information about potential aerial activity. Their effectiveness is enhanced when integrated with other counter-UAS technologies and established command-and-control arrangements.
The Vanquish Prime acquisition is therefore intended to strengthen the detection and tracking component of the wider defensive network rather than function as a standalone solution.
